Member (Tyler Kim): My claim says paid, but the money isn't in my account.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Tyler Kim, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Tyler Kim): It was a massage therapy claim for 120 dollars.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I can see why that's frustrating. Let me trace it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Tyler Kim): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Tyler Kim): I changed banks last month.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Which claim is it, and when was it approved?
Member (Tyler Kim): A massage therapy claim. It says approved on the 3rd.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Did you get a payment notification in the app?
Member (Tyler Kim): Yes, it says paid on the 4th, but nothing arrived.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Did you update it through the app or with your employer?
Member (Tyler Kim): Through my employer's payroll. I didn't know Sun Life was separate.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Let me take a look. I've checked the payment history and the direct deposit details on file.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Sun Life keeps its own direct deposit details, separate from your employer's payroll, so a change at work doesn't carry over.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I'm checking where the payment was sent and whether it came back.
Member (Tyler Kim): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The payment went to your old bank account and was returned. I've updated your direct deposit and reissued it, so it'll arrive within three business days.
Member (Tyler Kim): So I'll get it this time?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Yes. I've updated the account and reissued the payment, so it should land within three business days.
Member (Tyler Kim): Is there anything else going to the old account?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): No, all future claims will go to the new one.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): So the new account is on file and the 120-dollar payment is reissued. You'll see it within three business days.
Member (Tyler Kim): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-000006.transcript:
Member (Owen Martin): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Owen Martin, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Owen Martin): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Owen Martin): Yes, that's right.
Member (Owen Martin): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Owen Martin): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Is this the first request or a resubmission?
Member (Owen Martin): The second. The first was denied in July.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Has the dental office called us about this directly?
Member (Owen Martin): They said they called and got the same answer as me.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Are you in any pain right now?
Member (Owen Martin): Some. It's manageable, but I can't chew on that side.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the pre-authorization request and the documents received from the dental office.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The assessment is done against the plan's criteria for crowns, which are set by Health Canada.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I'm looking at the latest assessment on your file now.
Member (Owen Martin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Owen Martin): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Owen Martin): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Owen Martin): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Owen Martin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

SL-000370.transcript:
Member (Owen Morrison): I asked to transfer my pension from my old employer's plan to my bank and it still hasn't moved.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Owen Morrison, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Owen Morrison): The market's moved since then and I've lost money waiting.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Owen Morrison): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Owen Morrison): The receiving institution says they never got anything.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which plan is the transfer from?
Member (Owen Morrison): My old employer's pension plan. I left the company in May.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Where is the money going?
Member (Owen Morrison): To an RRSP at my bank. They say they're waiting on Sun Life.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): When did you send in the transfer request?
Member (Owen Morrison): In June. I signed everything they sent me.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Have you received any statement showing the transfer as pending?
Member (Owen Morrison): Only the annual statement, which still shows the balance with you.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've traced the transfer request and the paperwork on the plan account.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Your request came in on June 14. The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer authorization from the receiving institution, which is standard for locked-in pension money.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Until that form arrives, the funds stay invested in your current options, so they've moved with the market.
Member (Owen Morrison): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer form from the receiving institution. I can't release it until that arrives, but I've sent them a reminder.
Member (Owen Morrison): So I've lost money because of a form nobody told me about?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I understand. I've noted on your file that you've been waiting since June, so it's visible if this needs a review.
Member (Owen Morrison): Who follows up?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Retirement services will. I've asked them to call you once the form arrives.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: we're waiting on your bank's signed form, a reminder has gone to them today, and retirement services will call you when it's in.
Member (Owen Morrison): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Olivia Campbell): My claim says paid, but the money isn't in my account.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Hi Olivia Campbell, Marc Tremblay here — let me pull that up.

Agent (Marc Tremblay): How were you expecting to be paid?

Member (Olivia Campbell): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.

Member (Olivia Campbell): So I'll get it this time?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Yes. I've updated the account and reissued the payment, so it should land within three business days.
Member (Olivia Campbell): Is there anything else going to the old account?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): No, all future claims will go to the new one.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): So the new account is on file and the 120-dollar payment is reissued. You'll see it within three business days.
Member (Olivia Campbell): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Mei Roy): My Canadian Dental Care Plan crown request was denied and even the supervisor couldn't tell me why.

SL-000879.transcript:
Member (Hannah Cote): I cancelled my life insurance before it renewed and you still took the payment.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Hi Hannah Cote, Chloe Gagnon here — let me pull that up.
Member (Hannah Cote): I called two weeks before the renewal date to cancel.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Hannah Cote): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Hannah Cote): It went from about 250 to 750 dollars a month.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Which policy is this about?
Member (Hannah Cote): My term life policy. It renewed this month.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Did you get a confirmation of the cancellation?
Member (Hannah Cote): No, I was told it would be processed.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Is the payment still coming from the same bank account?
Member (Hannah Cote): Yes, same account.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): If the cost came down, would you want to keep some coverage?
Member (Hannah Cote): Maybe, if it's affordable.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the policy billing history and the forms received.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I can see your call from the 17th and the renewal payment taken on the 1st.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): The renewal rate is higher because the policy moved into a new age band on renewal.
Member (Hannah Cote): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): The premium increase follows the renewal schedule in your policy, so I can't change the rate. I can send you the renewal notice and your options, including reducing the coverage amount.
Member (Hannah Cote): Nobody told me it would triple.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): The notice went out 60 days before renewal, but I understand it's a shock at that size.
Member (Hannah Cote): How much would a lower amount cost?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Halving the coverage brings it to about 375 dollars a month. The comparison I'm sending shows a few options.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): To recap: the new rate follows the renewal schedule, I've sent you the notice and a lower-coverage option, and you can decide within 30 days.
Member (Hannah Cote): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.

Member (Tyler Martin): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Tyler Martin): Can I appeal it?

Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.

Agent (Priya Sandhu): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.

SL-001310.transcript:
Member (Owen Fortin): I want to check whether my plan covers orthodontics for my son.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Hi Owen Fortin, Kevin Nguyen here — let me pull that up.
Member (Owen Fortin): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Good question to ask before you commit. Let me look.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Owen Fortin): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Owen Fortin): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Is he listed as a dependant on your plan?
Member (Owen Fortin): Yes, since he was born.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): How old is he?
Member (Owen Fortin): Fourteen.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?
Member (Owen Fortin): They gave me an estimate of about six thousand dollars.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Let me take a look. I've checked the plan booklet and dependant coverage on the certificate.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Orthodontic coverage depends on your employer's plan, so I'm checking your certificate now.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.
Member (Owen Fortin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Orthodontics isn't part of your employer's plan. I can send you the booklet section, and your plan administrator at work can confirm whether that's changing.
Member (Owen Fortin): That's disappointing.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I understand. Some employers offer a health spending account that can be used for orthodontics.
Member (Owen Fortin): How would I check that?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): It would show under Accounts in the app. I don't see one on your certificate, but HR can confirm.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): To recap: orthodontics isn't in your employer's plan right now, and HR can tell you if that's changing.
Member (Owen Fortin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Hannah Singh): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Hannah Singh, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Hannah Singh): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Hannah Singh): Yes, that's right.
Member (Hannah Singh): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Hannah Singh): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Hannah Singh): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Hannah Singh): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Hannah Singh): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Hannah Singh): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Hannah Singh): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Hannah Singh): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Hannah Singh): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Hannah Roy): I've been off work for six weeks and still haven't had a decision on my short-term disability claim.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Hannah Roy, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Hannah Roy): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.

Member (Noah O'Brien): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Noah O'Brien): Yes, that's right.
Member (Noah O'Brien): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Noah O'Brien): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Noah O'Brien): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Noah O'Brien): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Noah O'Brien): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Noah O'Brien): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Noah O'Brien): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Noah O'Brien): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Noah O'Brien): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-001920.transcript:
Member (Mei Lavoie): My Canadian Dental Care Plan crown request was denied and even the supervisor couldn't tell me why.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Hi Mei Lavoie, Jasmine Wong here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mei Lavoie): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.

Member (Mei Lavoie): Yes, that's right.
Member (Mei Lavoie): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Mei Lavoie): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Is this the first request or a resubmission?
Member (Mei Lavoie): The second. The first was denied in July.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Has the dental office called us about this directly?
Member (Mei Lavoie): They said they called and got the same answer as me.

Member (Mei Lavoie): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Mei Lavoie): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Mei Lavoie): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Mei Lavoie): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Member (Mei Lavoie): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Olivia Lavoie): My son needs braces and I want to know what my plan pays before we commit.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Hi Olivia Lavoie, Aisha Rahman here — let me pull that up.
Member (Olivia Lavoie): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Happy to check that for you.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Olivia Lavoie): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Olivia Lavoie): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): How old is he?
Member (Olivia Lavoie): Fourteen.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?

Agent (Aisha Rahman): I understand. Some employers offer a health spending account that can be used for orthodontics.

Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Mathieu Kim, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mathieu Kim): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Mathieu Kim): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Mathieu Kim): The member ID is on the welcome letter.
Member (Mathieu Kim): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Did the letter mention any documents that were missing?
Member (Mathieu Kim): No, just that it doesn't meet the criteria.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Has the dental office called us about this directly?
Member (Mathieu Kim): They said they called and got the same answer as me.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Are you in any pain right now?
Member (Mathieu Kim): Some. It's manageable, but I can't chew on that side.

Agent (Sophie Belanger): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Mathieu Kim): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Mathieu Kim): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Mathieu Kim): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.
